notes:
Account summary
- Enterprise financial services customer (regulated workloads). Currently using Redwood for (a) support-agent/chat, (b) call/case summarization, and (c) internal doc search. Traffic mix includes streaming responses; they are sensitive to disconnects and tail latency spikes.
- Deployment preference: Dedicated today, evaluating Private (VPC) for tighter controls + audit requirements. Strong ask: multi-region resiliency with predictable behavior.

Current footprint (as captured in calls)
- Primary region: US-East. Secondary region preference: US-West.
- Data residency: US-only. Explicitly does NOT want automated spillover to EU.
- Wants the ability to pin model versions and have deterministic fallback model variant selection ("don’t silently change quality").

Regional reliability concerns (why this deal is escalated)
- They were customer-visible impacted by at least 2 regional events (timeframe per Support tickets below). Their leadership is now asking for: (1) clear failover policy, (2) proof of safety checks, (3) observable audit trail when failover decisions happen, and (4) comms plan.
- Quote from deep dive: "We can handle degraded quality; we can’t handle unannounced hard failures. We need degraded-but-available."

Support / incident references
- SUP-19240: Elevated 5xx + timeouts in US-East. They felt detection + mitigation was late; asked why traffic wasn’t shifted sooner.
- SUP-19288: Intermittent routing to a degraded region during partial impairment; asked for expected automatic failover behavior + SLAs for Dedicated.
- SUP-19312: Streaming disconnects correlated with regional packet loss; asked for guidance on retry/backoff + whether platform will auto-failover vs shed load.

Meetings / activities timeline
- 2025-02 (Support-led): initial escalation calls tied to SUP-19240; asked for timeline on reliability improvements.
- 2025-03-18: Enterprise technical deep dive on multi-region failover (Fireflies ff-48921). Attendees: Dev Patel (owner), Owen Phillips (SE), plus SRE/Platform observers. Topics: trigger signals, progressive failover, safety checks, audit logging, and what customers will see (HTTP errors vs increased latency vs model fallback).
- 2025-03-20: Follow-up assurance email sent (Gmail thread-2025-03-20-enterprise-escalation-assurance-on-failover). Requested: written summary they can forward to Risk + Procurement.

Requirements captured (must-haves)
- Multi-region resiliency:
  - Automatic detection of regional impairment (not just "region down") and earlier response (tail latency + error rate + network path signals).
  - Progressive failover: start with small % canary, expand by route/tier; ability to exclude certain endpoints.
  - Explicit anti-flap behavior: hysteresis + hold-down timers; manual override always available.
  - "Safe-to-failover" gating: proof secondary region has capacity headroom (GPU pool + queue depth) AND dependencies are healthy.
- Graceful degradation:
  - Prefer load shedding / tightened timeouts + controlled fallback model variants over full failover for partial impairment.
  - Customer-tier protections: their production traffic should not be deprioritized during a regional event.
- Observability + audit:
  - Audit log entries for failover decisions (what signal tripped, window, thresholds, who approved override).
  - Dashboard views they can reference during incidents (even if internal-only today, they want screenshots/shared readouts).
- Security/compliance:
  - SSO/SAML for console access.
  - Audit logging + retention controls (their baseline ask: 90 days, with option for longer).
  - KMS integration expectations for Private/VPC (customer-managed keys strongly preferred).

What we told them (positioning aligned to ongoing reliability program)
- We are executing a "regional failover automation upgrade" focused on:
  - Standardized health-signal aggregation (error rate, tail latency, dependency health, capacity saturation, network probes).
  - Automated trigger evaluation with hysteresis/hold-down timers and safety-guarded orchestration.
  - Progressive failover + clear rollback.
  - Better degraded-but-available behaviors (load shedding, timeouts, and model variant fallback).
- We were careful not to over-promise timing; shared that initial automated actions will roll out in guarded stages (monitor-only -> canary -> broader coverage) with strict change management.

Open questions / follow-ups to close
- Confirm if they require opt-in for any production controlled failover tests, or just advance notice + ability to exclude their account.
- Need a single-page assurance packet with:
  - Summary of triggers/signals, safety checks, and anti-flap controls (hysteresis + hold-down + manual override).
  - Expected customer-visible symptoms during impairment vs failover (including streaming behavior).
  - How we’ll communicate during controlled tests and real incidents (status page language + Support macros).
- Technical: review their retry policy for streaming disconnects; propose recommended client settings during degraded mode.

Internal notes (sales execution)
- This is likely a Dedicated expansion + Private/VPC add-on if we can satisfy GRC and resiliency requirements.
- Procurement will require written resiliency story + security artifacts; they will ask "what happens if us-east has packet loss but isn’t fully down".
- Strong preference for evidence: runbook excerpts, dashboard screenshots, and a clear statement that failover actions are auditable.

Next steps (owner)
- Dev Patel / Owen Phillips to send assurance packet + schedule 45-min follow-up with their platform lead + GRC.
- Coordinate with SRE/Platform to ensure our customer-facing narrative matches current automation rollout stage and avoids committing to full-auto failover everywhere.
